mainTopic: A daughter's and a widow's rights to support from the estate, how a widow loses that support, local customs, and whether a widow's clothes count against her כתובה
overview: The amud opens with a chain of questions about whether a daughter gets מזונות from her father's estate when her mother's כתובה is missing or not yet in force: a penalized mother, an ארוסה, and an אנוסה. All three end in תיקו. Next the גמרא turns to the widow's clause in the משנה. רב יוסף teaches that 'my house' does not include a hut, but she still keeps her support. Several אמוראים then list ways a widow loses support, such as agreeing to remarry, being unfaithful, or making herself up. The הלכה follows none of them. It follows שמואל: she loses support when she claims her כתובה in בית דין. רב and שמואל argue over whether the custom of יהודה or of גליל is the הלכה, and a story with רב נחמן shows that a woman follows her husband's place. They also argue whether a widow's clothes are appraised against her כתובה. רב נחמן and later רבינא rule like רב. The amud ends with cases about a father's instructions for his daughter's dowry, and the last case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two sides of the penalized-mother question, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides of the earlier question. Since the mother has no כתובה, maybe the daughter has no support either. Or maybe only the mother, who sinned, was penalized, and the innocent daughter was not. The question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she (the mother) has no כתובה, she (the daughter) has no support. Or perhaps: her mother, who did something forbidden, the רבנן penalized; but she (the daughter), who did nothing forbidden, the רבנן did not penalize. Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier question by explaining its two possible sides, and then admits it cannot decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says the daughter's support depends on the mother's כתובה, so once the כתובה is gone, the support is gone too. Side two says the penalty (קנס) was aimed only at the person who sinned, so it should not reach an innocent daughter. The question is never answered, so it ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Food and support; here, the daughter's support from her father's estate
Or perhaps; introduces the other side of a question
Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two women. The first 'she' (the one with no כתובה) is the mother. The one who gets or doesn't get מזונות is the daughter.

phrases.english: Since she has no marriage contract,
phrases.notes: This 'she' is the mother, whom the רבנן penalized by taking away her כתובה.

phrases.english: she (the daughter) has no support,
or perhaps: her mother, who did something forbidden,
the Sages penalized her,
but she (the daughter), who did nothing forbidden,
the Sages did not penalize her.
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלֵית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a question that began before this part of the daf by spelling out its two sides
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a penalty that takes away the mother's כתובה also take away the daughter's support?
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to look at it. Either the daughter's support is tied to the mother's כתובה, or a קנס only hits the person who sinned. The גמרא could not decide.

steps.title: רבא asks about the daughter of a betrothed woman
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a daughter born to a woman who was only betrothed (ארוסה) gets support from her father's estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: the daughter of a betrothed woman, does she get support, or does she not get support?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question about a different case. The גמרא will explain the two sides in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the father had only done אירוסין (the first stage of marriage) and then died, before the full marriage (נישואין). The question is whether the daughter's right to support already applies at this early stage.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; raises a question that needs to be decided
The daughter of a betrothed (not yet fully married) woman

phrases.english: Rava asked: a daughter of a betrothed woman,
does she get support,
or does she not get support?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the same chain about a daughter's support
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the daughter of an ארוסה get support from her father's estate?

steps.title: Two sides of רבא's question, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Since the mother has a כתובה, the daughter should get support. Or maybe not, since the רבנן made the כתובה take effect only at נישואין. The question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she has a כתובה, she gets support. Or perhaps, since the רבנן did not set up the כתובה until the time of full marriage, she does not get it. Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides of רבא's question and again cannot decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says the mother already has a כתובה, so the daughter's support, which is one of its promises, should apply. Side two says the רבנן's system of כתובה promises only begins at נישואין, so at the ארוסה stage nothing is in force yet.

keyTerms.meaning: They set up a rule (a תקנה)

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה — אִית לַהּ,
phrases.english: Since she has a marriage contract, she has (support),

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא תַּקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן כְּתוּבָּה
phrases.english: or perhaps: since the Sages did not institute the marriage contract
until the time of marriage, she does not have (support),
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of רבא's question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the כתובה's promises start at אירוסין or only at נישואין?
steps.whatToRemember: The question is when the כתובה's promises start. Is it as soon as there is a כתובה, or only at נישואין? No answer is given.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about the daughter of a woman who was raped
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the daughter of an אנוסה (a woman who was raped and then married by the man) gets support from his estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: the daughter of a woman who was raped, does she get support, or does she not get support?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a third question. The גמרא will next narrow down for whose opinion this question really matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אנוסה receives a fine (קנס) from the man, and he must marry her. The question is whether her daughter from him gets the usual support that comes with a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a woman who was raped and then married by the man

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked: a daughter of a raped woman,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת, אוֹ אֵין לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת?
phrases.english: does she get support, or does she not get support?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another new question in the same chain
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the daughter of an אנוסה get support from her father's estate?

steps.title: No question according to רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה there is nothing to ask. He holds that an אנוסה has a כתובה of a מנה, so the daughter gets support like any other daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, don't ask this, because he said she has a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the question does not even start according to one opinion. This sets up the next step, where the question is moved to a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother has a real כתובה, then all its promises, including the daughter's support, come with it. So for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה the answer is simply yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't ask it; there is no question here
A sum of 100 זוז, the standard כתובה of a non-virgin

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
do not ask it,
since he said she has a marriage contract of a maneh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב פפא's question by ruling out one opinion
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only rejects asking the question according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under his view the mother has a כתובה, so the daughter's support plainly applies

steps.title: The question is really according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The real question is according to the רבנן, who say the fine money takes the place of her כתובה. Does the daughter still get support?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where you should ask it is according to the רבנן, who say: the money of her fine counts as her כתובה. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves רב פפא's question to the opinion where it really matters and asks it again: what is the law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the fine already paid fills the role of her כתובה. So the question becomes: does the daughter's support survive when there is no separate כתובה, only the fine that replaced it?

keyTerms.meaning: Where you should ask it is
Fulfilled; took care of the obligation
The money of her fine (paid by the man who raped her)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the daughter's support depends on whether the mother truly has a כתובה. The question is whether something that only takes the place of a כתובה is enough.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Where you should ask is according to the Rabbis, who say:
the money of her fine fulfilled her marriage contract,
phrases.notes: He means the fine she already got counts as her כתובה, so she gets no separate כתובה payment.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, places the question according to the רבנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the רבנן, when the fine replaces the כתובה, does the daughter still get support?

steps.title: Two sides of the אנוסה question, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides of רב פפא's question. One side says no כתובה means no support. The other side says the reason for a כתובה does not apply here, so the daughter should still get support. The question stays as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the mother has no כתובה, maybe the daughter has no support. Or maybe: what is the reason for a כתובה? So that he will not find it easy to divorce her. But this man is not allowed to divorce her anyway. Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two sides of רב פפא's question about the daughter of an אנוסה. It cannot decide between them, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the daughter's support is one of the כתובה conditions, so if the mother has no כתובה, there is no support. Side two: the כתובה was made only to stop a husband from divorcing easily, and an אנוס is not allowed to divorce her at all. So her missing כתובה is not a real lack, and the conditions, including the daughter's support, may still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. It introduces the other side of a question.
Light in his eyes, meaning easy for him to send away
To send her out, meaning to divorce her
Let it stand. The question is left unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: The reason behind a כתובה is to make divorce costly. Where divorce is not allowed at all, as with an אנוס, the missing כתובה may not take away the conditions that come with it. Still, the question is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Since she does not have a marriage contract,
she does not have support,
phrases.notes: The first 'she' is the mother. This 'she' is the daughter.

phrases.english: or perhaps:
the marriage contract, what is its reason?
So that she will not be light in his eyes
to divorce her,
and this one, he cannot divorce her.
phrases.notes: The תורה says the man who forced her may never send her away (דברים 22:29).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלֵית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה, לֵית לַהּ מְזוֹנֵי, אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question raised in step 6 and closes it with תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the daughter's support depend on the mother actually having a כתובה, or on the reason behind the כתובה?

steps.title: A real house, not a hut, but she still gets support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the widow's clause from the משנה. רב יוסף teaches that 'my house' means a proper house and not a small hut, but the widow still keeps her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'You will dwell in my house, etc.' רב יוסף taught: 'In my house,' and not in my hut. But she does have support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה, the widow's right to live in her husband's house. רב יוסף explains how far that right goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'my house' limits her housing right. If the husband left only a tiny hut with no room for her, the heirs do not have to house her there. Even so, her right to food and support stays in place.

phrases.english: "You will dwell in my house," etc.
Rav Yosef taught:
"In my house," and not in my hut,
but she does have support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ תְּהֵא יָתְבָא בְּבֵיתִי וְכוּ׳. תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the widow's clause in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The housing right applies only to a proper house and not a hut. Her support continues either way.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: no support either
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי disagrees with רב יוסף. He says that a widow who does not live in the house loses her support too.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: She does not even have support.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion argues with רב יוסף's ruling from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To מר בר רב אשי, support and living in the husband's house go together. If she is not living there, even for this reason, she does not get support.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
She does not even have support.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מְזוֹנֵי נָמֵי לֵית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the second half of רב יוסף's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without living in the house, she gets no support.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow מר בר רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules against מר בר רב אשי, so the widow keeps her support, as רב יוסף taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like מר בר רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument from the last two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the halacha is not like מר בר רב אשי, רב יוסף's view stands. She has no claim to live in a hut, but she still receives support.
steps.whatToRemember: A widow whose husband's 'house' is too small to live in still gets her support from the heirs.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: And the halacha is not like Mar bar Rav Ashi.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the argument between steps 8 and 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The widow keeps her support even when she cannot live in the house.

steps.title: A widow who agrees to remarry loses support
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting שמואל, rules that once a widow agrees to a marriage proposal, she loses her support from her late husband's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: If men asked her to marry and she agreed, she has no support.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule begins about when a widow loses her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her support exists because she stays connected to her late husband's home. Once she agrees to marry someone else, even before the wedding, she has shown she is moving on, so the support stops.

keyTerms.meaning: She agreed, she was won over

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
If they asked her to marry and she agreed,
she has no support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּבָעוּהָ לְהִנָּשֵׂא וְנִתְפַּיְּיסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: when a widow loses her support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Agreeing to remarry ends a widow's support.

steps.title: Does refusing always keep her support?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the opposite conclusion from שמואל's words: if she did not agree, does she always keep her support?
steps.simpleTranslation: So if she did not agree, she does have support?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads שמואל's rule in reverse and asks whether that reading is right. This sets up רב ענן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, שמואל's rule suggests that any refusal keeps her support. The גמרא questions whether every kind of refusal really counts.

keyTerms.meaning: So then. It introduces the opposite conclusion drawn from a statement.

phrases.english: So if she did not agree,
she has support?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לֹא נִתְפַּיְּיסָה, יֵשׁ לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reverse conclusion from step 11's rule and questions it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does every refusal keep her support, or only some kinds?

steps.title: It depends on why she refused
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן reports what שמואל told him directly. If she refused out of loyalty to her late husband, she keeps her support. If she refused only because the men were not suitable for her, she loses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: שמואל explained it to me himself. If she said, 'Because of so-and-so, my husband,' she has support. If she said, 'Because these men are not suitable for me,' she has no support.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן answers the question by passing on שמואל's own explanation: what matters is the reason she gave for refusing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refusing out of loyalty to her late husband shows she is still tied to his home, so her support continues. Refusing only because the man was not good enough shows she does want to remarry, so she is treated like one who agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally

steps.whatToRemember: In שמואל's view as רב ענן reports it, what matters is the reason she refused. Loyalty to her late husband keeps her support, while turning down an unsuitable man does not. Step 17 later rules that the הלכה does not follow these teachings.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: It was explained to me personally by Mar Shmuel:
If she said, "Because of so-and-so, my husband,"
phrases.notes: She means her late husband. She refuses out of loyalty to him.

phrases.english: she has support,
if she said, "Because of people who are not suitable for her,"
she has no support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by splitting refusals into two kinds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Refusing out of loyalty to her late husband keeps her support. Refusing because the man is not suitable does not.

steps.title: An unfaithful widow loses support
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a widow who is unfaithful loses her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: If she was unfaithful, she has no support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another case in which a widow loses her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her support depends on her staying connected to her late husband's home. Being unfaithful breaks that connection, so the support stops.

keyTerms.meaning: She was unfaithful, she had forbidden relations

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
If she was unfaithful, she has no support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: זִינְּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way a widow can lose her support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unfaithful widow loses her support.

steps.title: A widow who makes herself up loses support
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a widow who paints her eyes and dyes her hair loses her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If she painted her eyes and dyed her hair, she has no support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more case in which a widow loses her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making herself up shows she is trying to attract men in order to remarry. She is acting like someone moving on from her late husband's home, so she loses support, much like one who agreed to a match.

keyTerms.meaning: She dyed or styled her hair, she made herself up

steps.whatToRemember: These opinions share one idea: a widow keeps her support only while she acts as part of her late husband's home. The next step shows that רב יוסף's view does not have to include unfaithfulness. Step 17 then rules that the הלכה follows none of these opinions.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If she painted her eyes and dyed her hair, she has no support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כִּיחֲלָה וּפִירְכְּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final case to the list of ways a widow loses support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow who makes herself up to attract men loses her support.

steps.title: How the two rulings about losing support relate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares רב חסדא and רב יוסף. Whoever says unfaithfulness costs her support would surely say makeup does too. But whoever says makeup costs her support might say unfaithfulness does not, because temptation overpowered her.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says a widow who was unfaithful loses her support, all the more so if she painted her eyes and dyed her hair. According to the one who says painting and dyeing make her lose it, if she was unfaithful she still has support. Why? Her desire overpowered her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the two rulings from Steps 14 and 15. It explains which ruling includes the other, and why one of them might not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Makeup shows a calm, planned wish to remarry, so it clearly ends her tie to her late husband. Unfaithfulness may be a moment of weakness and not a decision to move on. So the makeup opinion does not have to agree that unfaithfulness costs her support.

keyTerms.meaning: she painted her eyes and dyed her hair

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that the 'worse' act keeps her support. The question here is not how bad the act is. The question is whether she showed a real decision to move on from her late husband.

phrases.english: The one who says "she was unfaithful" (loses support)
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא from Step 14.

phrases.english: all the more so if she painted her eyes and dyed her hair
The one who says "she painted and dyed" (loses support)
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף from Step 15.

phrases.english: but if she was unfaithful, she still has support
What is the reason?
Her desire overpowered her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר זִינְּתָה, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן כִּיחֲלָה וּפִירְכְּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes how the rulings in Steps 14 and 15 relate to each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The unfaithfulness opinion surely includes makeup. The makeup opinion does not have to include unfaithfulness, because her desire overpowered her.

steps.title: The final ruling: claiming her כתובה in court ends support
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows none of the earlier opinions. It follows רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: a widow who claims her כתובה in בית דין loses her מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is not like any of these teachings. Rather, it is like what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a woman who claims her כתובה in court does not get support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside all the opinions from Steps 11 through 16. It gives the final practical rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is no longer engagement, makeup or unfaithfulness. The test is a formal act: going to בית דין to collect her כתובה. That act shows she is ending her financial tie to the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman who claims her כתובה payment

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a widow loses her support from the estate when she claims her כתובה in בית דין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה about when a widow's support from the estate ends.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is not like any of these teachings,
phrases.notes: This covers all the opinions back to Step 11.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: rather, it is like what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
a woman who claims her כתובה in court
does not get support.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּכֹל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects all the earlier opinions and gives the final הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A widow who claims her כתובה in בית דין loses her מזונות.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say claiming does not end support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists selling, pledging, or setting aside her כתובה as ways she loses support, but it does not list claiming it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't she get support? But a ברייתא teaches: if she sold her כתובה, pledged it, or made it a security for someone else, she gets no support. These cases, yes. But claiming it, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to argue with שמואל's ruling from Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only cases where she gave away rights in her כתובה. Because claiming is left off the list, it sounds like claiming does not cost her support. That contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: property set aside to pay a specific debt

phrases.english: And she does not get support?!
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
If she sold her כתובה,
or pledged her כתובה,
or made her כתובה a security set aside for someone else,
she does not get support.
In these cases, yes (she loses it),
but if she claims it, no!
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own reading of the ברייתא. It is not part of the ברייתא itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of שמואל accepted in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that claiming her כתובה ends her support
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only selling, pledging and setting aside. That suggests claiming does not end her support.

steps.title: The difference is court versus outside court
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's cases end support whether or not they happen in court. Claiming ends support only when it is done in court. That is why the ברייתא left claiming off its general list.
steps.simpleTranslation: These cases make her lose support whether done in court or not in court. Claiming makes her lose it in court, yes. Not in court, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It reads the ברייתא's silence about claiming in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only lists acts that cost her support in every setting. Claiming works only in בית דין, so it did not belong on that list. שמואל, who spoke only about claiming in court, still stands.

keyTerms.term: בֵּין בְּבֵית דִּין בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין
keyTerms.meaning: whether in court or not in court

steps.whatToRemember: Selling, pledging or setting aside her כתובה ends support anywhere. Claiming her כתובה ends support only when done in בית דין.

phrases.english: These cases make her lose support, whether done in court
or not in court.
Claiming: in court, yes (she loses support),
not in court, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי, בֵּין בְּבֵית דִּין בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18 and defends שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading what the ברייתא left out: a difference between in court and outside court
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא left out claiming because claiming never costs her support.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא left out claiming because claiming costs her support only in בית דין, while its listed cases cost it everywhere.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue over whose custom is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the custom of ירושלים. רב rules like אנשי יהודה and שמואל rules like אנשי גליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And this is how the people of ירושלים would write, etc.' It was stated: רב said the הלכה follows the people of יהודה. שמואל said the הלכה follows the people of גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה about two local customs for a widow's support. It reports that רב and שמואל disagree about which custom is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In גליל and ירושלים, the widow is supported from the estate for as long as she stays a widow. In יהודה, the heirs can end her support by paying her כתובה. רב follows יהודה, so the heirs can pay her off. שמואל follows גליל, so she keeps her support.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of יהודה, whose custom let the heirs pay off the widow
The people of גליל, whose custom gave the widow support for her whole widowhood

steps.confusionAlert: רב sides with יהודה, not ירושלים. In the משנה, ירושלים and גליל share the same custom, so שמואל is effectively siding with both of them.

phrases.english: And this is how the people of Jerusalem would [write], etc.
It was stated: Rav said:
The halacha follows the people of Judea,
and Shmuel said:
The halacha follows the people of the Galilee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, רַב אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּאַנְשֵׁי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of losing support by claiming the כתובה to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the הלכה follows אנשי יהודה (the heirs can end support by paying the כתובה). שמואל: the הלכה follows אנשי גליל (support lasts through her widowhood).

steps.title: Which regions follow רב and which follow שמואל
steps.stepSummary: בבל and its towns follow רב. נהרדעא and its towns follow שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: בבל and all its towns act like רב. נהרדעא and all its towns act like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how people actually practiced. Each region followed the local master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute was not settled with one ruling for everyone. Each area kept the ruling of its own רב, so a widow's rights depended on where she lived.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonia, here meaning the region where רב's view was followed

phrases.english: Babylonia and all its surrounding towns act like Rav,
Neharde'a and all its surrounding towns act like Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּבֶל וְכֹל פַּרְווֹדֶהָא נְהוּג כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells us how the dispute in Step 20 was practiced in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Practice follows the region: בבל like רב, נהרדעא like שמואל.

steps.title: A woman from מחוזא married into נהרדעא comes to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A woman from מחוזא who married a man from נהרדעא came before רב נחמן. He recognized from her accent that she was from מחוזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman from מחוזא who was married into נהרדעא. They came before רב נחמן. He heard from her voice that she was from מחוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that tests the rule about regions. This line sets the scene for רב נחמן's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that this woman belongs to two places. She comes from מחוזא, which follows רב, but she married into נהרדעא, which follows שמואל. Which place decides her rights?

keyTerms.meaning: Mechoza, a town in the region that followed רב

phrases.english: There was a certain woman from Mechoza
who was married into Neharde'a.
They came before Rav Nachman,
he heard her voice
[and recognized] that she was from Mechoza.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא בַּת מָחוֹזָא דַּהֲוָת נְסִיבָא לִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the regional rule from Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: a woman from a רב region married into a שמואל region.

steps.title: רב נחמן first rules by her hometown
steps.stepSummary: Since she is from מחוזא, רב נחמן says the practice of בבל applies, which follows רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: בבל and all its towns act like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his first ruling, based on where the woman comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He treats her hometown as the deciding factor. By רב's view, the heirs can end her support by paying her כתובה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Babylonia and all its surrounding towns act like Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: בָּבֶל וְכׇל פַּרְווֹדֶהָא נְהוּג כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the regional rule from Step 21 to the case in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First ruling: go by her hometown, so רב's view applies.

steps.title: But she married into נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: The people there object that she married into נהרדעא, so maybe her husband's place should decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But she married into נהרדעא!
steps.whatsHappening: The people in the case push back on רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that a wife's rights may depend on her husband's place, not her hometown. If so, נהרדעא's practice, which follows שמואל, should apply.

phrases.english: They said to him:
But she married into Neharde'a!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לִנְהַרְדְּעָא נְסִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that her hometown's practice applies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She married into נהרדעא, so her husband's place, not her hometown, may be what counts.

steps.title: רב נחמן agrees: then נהרדעא's practice applies
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן accepts the point. If she married into נהרדעא, she follows נהרדעא's practice, which is like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If so, נהרדעא and all its towns act like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן changes his ruling based on the new fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's place decides, not where the woman grew up. So this widow keeps her support as long as she stays a widow, like שמואל.
steps.whatToRemember: A married woman follows the practice of her husband's place, not her hometown.

phrases.english: He said to them: If so,
Neharde'a and all its surrounding towns act like Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from Step 24 and changes the ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the objection and changes the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her hometown (מחוזא) decides, so רב's view applies.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her husband's place (נהרדעא) decides, so שמואל's view applies.

steps.title: How far does נהרדעא extend
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the borders of the נהרדעא region are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how far does נהרדעא extend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since practice depends on region, we need to know exactly which towns count as part of נהרדעא's area.

phrases.english: And up to where is [the region of] Neharde'a?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד הֵיכָא נְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the borders of the region mentioned in Steps 21 and 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The geographic limit of the area that follows נהרדעא's practice.

steps.title: Wherever נהרדעא's קב measure is used
steps.stepSummary: The region of נהרדעא reaches as far as people use the קב measure of נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As far as the קב of נהרדעא is used.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about borders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The border is not marked on a map. Any place that uses נהרדעא's system of measures counts as its area, so it follows שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב, a unit of volume measure

phrases.english: Up to where the kav of Neharde'a is used.
phrases.notes: A קב is a measuring unit. Places using נהרדעא's measures count as its area.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד הֵיכָא דְּסָגֵי קַבָּא דִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נהרדעא's area includes every place that uses its קב measure.

steps.title: Is a widow's clothing counted against her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute. רב says the court appraises the clothes the widow is wearing. שמואל says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about a widow: רב said, we appraise what she is wearing. שמואל said, we do not appraise what she is wearing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new dispute between רב and שמואל. The question is whether a widow's clothes are counted when she collects her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that the value of the clothes she has on is taken off her כתובה payment. שמואל holds that her clothes are not counted, so she gets the full amount.

keyTerms.meaning: What is on her, meaning her clothes

phrases.english: It was stated: A widow,
Rav said: We appraise what is on her.
phrases.notes: He means the clothes she is wearing. Their value is taken off her כתובה.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
We do not appraise what is on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר. אַלְמָנָה, רַב אָמַר: שָׁמִין מַה שֶּׁעָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new dispute between the same two אמוראים, now about a widow's clothes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a widow's clothes are appraised and taken off her כתובה. שמואל: they are not appraised.

steps.title: For a hired worker, the opinions are reversed
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין reports that with a hired worker, רב and שמואל switch sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said: And with a hired worker it is the reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין adds a related case where רב and שמואל hold the opposite positions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a hired worker, רב says his clothes are not appraised and taken off his wages, and שמואל says they are. In the next step, רב כהנא gives a different version, with no switch of sides.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix them up. With the widow, רב appraises and שמואל does not. With the worker, רב does not appraise and שמואל does.

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin said:
And the reverse is so with a hired worker.
phrases.notes: With the worker, רב says we don't appraise his clothes and שמואל says we do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין: וְחִילּוּפָהּ בְּלָקִיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case where the positions from Step 28 are switched.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a hired worker: רב does not appraise the clothes, and שמואל does.

steps.title: רב כהנא's version: no switch for a hired worker
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא teaches that with a לקיט, רב and שמואל keep the same sides as with the widow. He gives a memory sign for רב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא taught: the same is true for a hired worker. He gave a memory sign: 'Orphan and widow, take off and go out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a different report from רב חייא בר אבין. He says the dispute about the worker matches the dispute about the widow, with no switching of sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the step before, רב חייא בר אבין said that with a worker, רב and שמואל trade positions. רב כהנא disagrees: רב still says the clothes are appraised, and שמואל still says they are not. The memory sign puts the 'orphan', meaning the poor worker, together with the widow, since both must 'take off' their clothes for appraisal in רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches, or reports a version of the teaching
a hired worker, such as someone hired to gather produce
a memory sign that helps you remember who holds which view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reports. רב חייא בר אבין says the sides switch for a worker. רב כהנא says they stay the same.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana teaches:
And likewise with a hired worker.
And he puts a memory sign on it:
"Orphan and widow, take off and go out."
phrases.notes: The 'orphan' stands for the poor worker. 'Take off' hints at רב's view that their clothes get appraised.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא מַתְנֵי: וְכֵן בְּלָקִיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version from רב חייא בר אבין's report about the hired worker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a hired worker, רב says the clothes are appraised and שמואל says they are not, just as with the widow.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רב despite a משנה that seems to follow שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules like רב, even though he admits that a משנה in ערכין seems to follow שמואל. He quotes that משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Even though a משנה seems to follow שמואל, the הלכה is like רב. The משנה says that when a man consecrates his property or pledges his own value to the Temple, the Temple cannot take his wife's clothes, his children's clothes, clothes he dyed for them, or new sandals he bought for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the final ruling for the widow's clothes: we follow רב. At the same time, he points to a משנה that looks like it supports שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the Temple treasurer cannot collect the wife's clothing from the husband's property. That suggests the clothes belong to her and not to him, which sounds like שמואל. Even so, רב נחמן says the הלכה is like רב, and this sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: one who gives all his property to the Temple
one who pledges his own fixed value, his ערך, to the Temple

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling of the סוגיא: the widow's clothes are appraised, as רב says.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Even though we learned in a Mishnah
in line with Shmuel,
the halacha is like Rav.
As we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in ערכין 24a.

phrases.english: Both one who consecrates his property,
and one who pledges his own value
has no claim on his wife's clothing,
phrases.notes: He means the Temple treasurer cannot collect these items.

phrases.english: nor on his children's clothing,
nor on dyed clothing that he dyed for them,
nor on new sandals that he bought for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דִּתְנַן בְּמַתְנִיתִין כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the widow dispute from step 28 and gives the final ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רב: the clothes the widow is wearing are appraised, even though the משנה in ערכין seems to follow שמואל.

steps.title: רבא asks why the הלכה is not like the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: if a משנה follows שמואל, how can the הלכה follow רב?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Since a משנה follows שמואל, why is the הלכה like רב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן's ruling. Normally we would not rule against a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's view cannot simply override a משנה. If the משנה really supports שמואל, ruling like רב looks impossible. רבא wants רב נחמן to explain this.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
But since we learned a Mishnah
in line with Shmuel,
why is the halacha like Rav?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דִּתְנַן מַתְנִיתִין כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אַמַּאי הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling from the step before.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You cannot rule against a משנה, and this משנה seems to support שמואל.

steps.title: A careful reading shows the משנה fits רב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה only looks like שמואל on a quick reading. A careful look shows it fits רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: At first glance it seems to follow שמואל. When you look into it carefully, the הלכה is like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. He says the משנה does not really support שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording seems to point toward שמואל, but that is only the surface meaning. Once you understand the reason behind the משנה, it fits with רב. The next step explains that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: at first glance, on the surface

phrases.english: He said to him:
At first glance it runs like Shmuel;
when you look into it carefully,
the halacha is like Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְאוֹרָה כִּשְׁמוּאֵל רְהִיטָא, כִּי מְעַיְּינַתְּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the משנה's surface meaning is not its real meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows the wife's clothes are fully hers, as שמואל says.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read carefully, the משנה fits רב.

steps.title: The reason: he gave her the clothes so she would stay with him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: the husband gives his wife ownership of the clothes only while she stays with him. He never gave them to her so she could take them and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? When he gave her ownership, it was so she would stay with him. He did not give it to her so she could take it and leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה fits רב. Her ownership of the clothes depends on her staying married to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the couple is together, the clothes count as hers, so the Temple treasurer cannot take them. That is the משנה's case. When she leaves, as a widow does, the husband never meant for her to keep them. So they count as his and are appraised against her כתובה, just as רב says.

keyTerms.meaning: with the intention, on the understanding
to stay with him, literally to stand before him

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רב: the widow's clothes are appraised against her כתובה. The משנה in ערכין fits this, because the husband gives his wife the clothes only on the understanding that she stays with him, not so she can take them and leave.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
When he gave her ownership,
it was on the understanding that she stay with him.
On the understanding that she take them and leave
he did not give her ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? כִּי אַקְנִי לַהּ, אַדַּעְתָּא לְמֵיקַם קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב נחמן's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה is talking about a wife who is still with her husband.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife owns the clothes no matter what happens.
steps.terutzMaskana: She owns them only while she stays with him. Once she leaves, they are appraised, as רב says.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like רב, and the משנה is fully consistent with this.

steps.title: A widow sues the orphans and wears all her clothes to court
steps.stepSummary: A widow from the family of בר אלישיב claims her כתובה from the orphans. They say it is embarrassing for her to go to court in plain clothes, so she puts on all her clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter-in-law of the בר אלישיב family was claiming her כתובה from the orphans. As she was taking them to court, they told her: 'It is embarrassing for us that you go dressed like this.' So she went and put on all her clothes, covering herself with every garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story about a widow's court case. This story sets up a ruling that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that matters is that she ends up wearing all her clothes. The earlier steps argued about whether a widow's clothes are counted toward her כתובה. So what she is wearing in court will decide how much she actually collects.

keyTerms.meaning: it is demeaning / embarrassing for us

phrases.english: The daughter-in-law of the house of Bar Elyashiv
was claiming her marriage contract payment from the orphans.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא מַמְטְיָא לְהוּ לְבֵי דִינָא,
phrases.english: She was bringing them to court.
They said: It is demeaning for us
that you should go like this.
phrases.notes: "Like this" means in her everyday house clothes.

phrases.english: She went and put them on
and covered herself with all of the clothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּלְּתָא דְּבֵי בַּר אֶלְיָשִׁיב הֲוָה קָא תָּבְעָה כְּתוּבְּתַהּ מִיַּתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling that the הלכה follows רב, the גמרא brings a real case where that rule gets applied.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The facts are laid out: the widow comes to court wearing all of her clothes.

steps.title: רבינא rules like רב: the clothes she wears are appraised
steps.stepSummary: The case comes before רבינא. He rules like רב: a widow's clothes are appraised and counted toward her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבינא. He told them: The הלכה follows רב, who said that for a widow, we appraise whatever she is wearing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא decides the case using רב's rule. Everything the widow is wearing is valued and counted as part of her כתובה payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because she came wearing all her clothes, all of them get appraised, and their value is taken off what the orphans owe her. This confirms in a real case what רב נחמן said earlier: the הלכה follows רב.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the הלכה follows רב: a widow's clothes are appraised and counted toward her כתובה.

phrases.english: They came before Ravina.
He said to them: The halacha follows Rav,
who said: For a widow, we appraise what is on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבִינָא, אֲמַר לְהוּ: הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the story told in step 35.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב: everything a widow is wearing is appraised as part of her כתובה.

steps.title: The dowry got cheaper: the savings go to the orphans
steps.stepSummary: A man's will said to give his daughter a dowry. Dowry prices then dropped. רב אידי בר אבין rules that the savings go to the orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man told his heirs: 'Give my daughter a dowry.' Then the cost of a dowry went down. רב אידי בר אבין said: The savings belong to the orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case about inheritance. A dowry becomes cheaper, and רב אידי בר אבין decides who keeps the money that was saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter gets the dowry itself, meaning the usual items, not a fixed amount of money. So when prices drop, the leftover money is not hers. It stays with the orphans, who are the heirs.
steps.confusionAlert: Here, "orphans" means the man's sons who inherit his estate. The daughter is not included in that word.

phrases.english: A certain man said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means his heirs. He is giving instructions for after he dies.

phrases.english: "A dowry for my daughter."
The dowry became cheaper.
Rav Idi bar Avin said:
The profit goes to the orphans.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ: נְדוּנְיָא לִבְרַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the widow's clothes to a new case about a daughter's dowry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a dowry becomes cheaper, the savings belong to the orphans, not to the daughter.

steps.title: Opening of another case about a man's will
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins another story about what a man told his heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: This line just opens the next case. The גמרא is setting up a new story, and the rest of it comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording matches the opening of the dowry case. That tells us another inheritance instruction is coming. The actual details and ruling come in the next lines.

phrases.english: A certain man said to them:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case in the same style as the dowry case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only sets up the next case.
